producer_report.summary: I changed D43 matching in `judge` so a cited command counts as seen when it is a whole simple command inside a command the verifier ran. I could not read the failing jobs' logs, so I inferred this cause from the code. A new splitter breaks both the ran and the cited commands on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` and newlines, never inside quotes. It also collapses whitespace outside quotes and drops a trailing `2>&1`. A cited command is seen only if every simple command in it was run. A different argument, filter or package is still unseen, and so is a command never run. Those still leave the criterion unmet with "cited but not seen running". Two new unit tests cover run alone, after `&&`, piped to `tail`, extra whitespace, other filter or package, prefix, quoted text, empty and never-run. I added D63, which amends D43 and says why the earlier producer-brief decision (D62) could not fix a matcher problem. It cites no commit hash. I also updated the verifier prompt, the D43 paragraph in the v0 design, and the CHANGELOG under Changed. The full test run, clippy and fmt all passed.

checks_run.note: all crates, including the policy tests
applied formatting; I did not run --check separately afterwards

open_issues: The cause is inferred from the code, not from the verifier's command logs, which were absent.
I did not touch policy.rs or lifecycle.rs. The tests showed no gap, and the existing lifecycle test for a never-run cited command passes.
The splitter is simple and is not a full shell parser. Heredocs and `$(...)` are not handled. Policy denies those anyway.
mistakes: My first version failed my own 'piped to tail' test: a ran piece ending in `2>&1` did not equal the cited bare command. I fixed it by dropping a trailing `2>&1` from both sides.
learnings: `cargo test` stops at the first failing crate unless --no-fail-fast is given.
Verifier commands may include `2>&1`, which policy.rs allows. Matching has to tolerate it.
The enforcement-map policy test requires that tests named in decisions.md exist.
desires: The failing jobs' verifier command logs, to confirm the inferred cause.
